brief: The market is the last flat system in the town: three stalls, every fourth day, identical in February and August. Fifty feet away the allotments now ripen, are picked, rest and re-sow across a full year, gardeners arrive at a rate that reads ripePlots(), and they walk out carrying a basket (a.crop) that goes nowhere. Connect them — what the stalls carry should follow what the plots have actually produced, so a February market is thin and root-heavy and an August one is full. Why now: it is the best remaining "these two systems should know about each other" in the town, and the lane has had nothing since #18.
successLooksLike: Two market mornings pinned six months apart are visibly different stalls, and a probe can name which plots the difference came from.
avoid: Do not add a fourth stall type — three exist and the census says they are under-used. Do not give the market its own arrival source; it already has a spawn band under laneCap, and the whole east half competes for that one budget. Watch the autumn shoulder: bloomCap is stepped 3/2/1 while everything around it lerps (c50), so a market driven off ripeness will inherit that cliff.
